paper_sections.title: Emotion regulation in social anxiety disorder: behavioral and neural responses to three socio-emotional tasks
Brain responses: BOLD signal temporal dynamics

description.value: The study examined behavioral and fMRI BOLD responses during cognitive reappraisal of three socio-emotional stimulus types in generalized social anxiety disorder and healthy controls.

spans.text: The goal of the present study was to examine behavioral and fMRI BOLD responses in patients with SAD compared to healthy controls (HC) when reappraising socio-emotional stimuli.

design.value: A between-group fMRI study comparing 27 unmedicated adults with generalized SAD with 27 healthy controls during three socio-emotional tasks, each containing React and Reappraise conditions.

spans.text: Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) of blood oxygen-level dependent (BOLD) signal, we examined reappraisal-related behavioral and neural responses in 27 participants with generalized SAD and 27 healthy controls (HC) during three socio-emotional tasks: (1) looming harsh faces (Faces); (2) videotaped actors delivering social criticism (Criticism); and (3) written autobiographical negative self-beliefs (Beliefs).
To assess social anxiety symptom severity, participants completed the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale-Self-Report (LSAS-SR) [ ].

task_description.value: Participants viewed looming harsh faces and either reacted normally or reappraised their emotion.

spans.text: Participants were trained prior to the baseline scan to either react to the faces by engaging in the picture (‘Just let yourself feel’) and thinking: ‘This person is upset with me; angry with me’, or to reappraise their emotion, for example by thinking: ‘Maybe this person just had a bad day’.
All tasks were programmed in Eprime (Psychology Software Tools, Inc.).

instructions.value: React normally without attempting to control, modify, or regulate reactions; or try to down regulate negative emotion reactions by actively reinterpreting the meaning of the emotion inducing stimulus.

spans.text: During the ‘Reappraise’ condition, participants were instructed to try and down regulate negative emotion reactions by actively reinterpreting the meaning of the emotion inducing stimulus.

task_description.value: Participants watched videotaped actors delivering social criticism or praise and either reacted or reframed their reaction; only the social criticism evaluation period was analyzed.

spans.text: For the current study, only the 7.5-s evaluation period of the social criticism trials were included in the analysis.
All tasks were programmed in Eprime (Psychology Software Tools, Inc.).

instructions.value: React to the social criticism by reflecting on how the statement represents something true about themselves, or reappraise their emotion by thinking: ‘this is not always true’, or ‘this is only a thought, not a fact’.
